messages:
Carla M.: Pushed marmot-v1 (embed) to staging with int8 dynamic quant. Quick smoke: recall@10 down ~3.7% vs oak-baseline on short-tail queries.
Ben G.: Which quant path exactly? dynamic vs perchannel?
Carla M.: Dynamic via our onnxruntime pipeline (calibration skipped). Serving config: batch=128, max_seq=48.
Priya S.: Skipping calibration could explain bias. Short queries are sensitive to tokenization normalization too.
Noah R.: Do we apply final L2 norm at export and again at index time? Double norm kills distances.
Carla M.: Index pipeline does L2. Export default includes final norm layer. I can export a strip-norm variant.
embed-bot: auto-eval: recall@1/5/10 = [0.61,0.73,0.802], baseline oak fp16 recall@10=0.839
Carla M.: Running ablations: A) fp16 export, B) int8-perchannel with 256-sample calibration, C) eval with oak tokenizer.
Ben G.: Add per-length buckets (<=8, 9-32, >32) and centroid NN gap. If the drop is only <=8 then tokenize/pooling likely.
Priya S.: Also collect cosine vs L2 ranking comparison; quant can distort norms.
Carla M.: Will run overnight sweep (20k queries stratified). Posting results AM and will include export artifacts and ONNX graph diff.
Noah R.: If perchannel calibrated int8 recovers most of the gap, we can update default pipeline. Thanks! :thumbsup:
